items.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 13 at 8:12AM PST until November 17 at 3:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf. For the High Surf
Advisory, large breaking waves of 4 to 7 feet this afternoon
through evening, increasing to 8 to 14 feet Friday through
Tuesday. Peak surf heights expected Saturday, possibly peaking
again Monday.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 3 PM PST Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can
wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats
nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of significant west- northwesterly
swells are expected to produce large surf into next week with
highest surf and greatest impacts likely peaking Saturday and
potentially again Monday. There is potential for moderate
coastal flooding impacts at times, especially Saturday. Some of
these impacts may be significant beach erosion and shallow
flooding of normal dry beaches and walkways. Breaking waves are
possible at the Ventura Harbor entrance during peak surf. There
is a low chance for warning level surf Saturday.
items.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

items.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued November 13 at 2:11AM PST until November 15 at 3:00AM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
items.description:
* WHAT...Hazardous sea conditions.

* WHERE...East Santa Barbara Channel from Pt. Conception to Pt.
Mugu CA including Santa Cruz Island.

* WHEN...From 6 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...See the Coastal Waters Forecast (CWFLOX)
for more.
items.instruction:
Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller
vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions.
